facts.value: Horses are prey animals with a strong fight-or-flight response.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Their first reaction to a threat is to startle and usually flee, although they will stand their ground and defend themselves when flight is impossible or if their young are threatened.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: They also tend to be curious; when startled, they will often hesitate an instant to ascertain the cause of their fright, and may not always flee from something that they perceive as non-threatening.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Most light horse riding breeds were developed for speed, agility, alertness, and endurance, natural qualities that extend from their wild ancestors.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Through selective breeding, some breeds of horses are quite docile, particularly certain draft horses.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Horses are herd animals, with a clear hierarchy of rank, led by a dominant individual, usually a mare.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: They are social creatures that are able to form companionship attachments to their own species and to other animals, including humans.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: They communicate in various ways, including vocalizations such as nickering or whinnying, mutual grooming, and body language.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: Many horses will become difficult to manage if they are isolated.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: With training, horses can learn to accept a human as a companion, and thus be comfortable away from other horses.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science

facts.value: When confined with insufficient companionship, exercise, or stimulation, individuals may develop stable vices, an assortment of bad habits, mostly stereotypies of psychological origin, that include wood chewing, wall kicking, 'weaving' (rocking back and forth), and other problems.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Equine Science
